column4: 暑假期间，他去了很多地方。
column5: During the summer holiday, he went to many places.
column6: 期间 means the period while something lasts: 放假期间 (during the holiday), 比赛期间 (during the match). It follows the event.

column5: Everyone has arrived.
column6: 齐 means "all together, complete" (到齐了, 齐了) and "neat" (整齐). 东西备齐了 means everything is ready.

column5: One of them is my friend.
column6: 其 is a written pronoun meaning "his, her, its, their, that". It is mostly used in set words: 其中 (among them), 其他 (other), 其实 (actually), 其次 (second).

column5: This is a miracle.
column6: 奇迹 is a miracle or a wonder: 创造奇迹 (to create a miracle), 出现奇迹 (a miracle happens). 奇 means strange.

column4: 我吃了一个，其余的给你。
column5: I ate one, and the rest is for you.
column6: 其余 means "the rest": 其余的人 (the rest of the people), 其余的东西 (the other things).

column5: He works for a big company.
column6: 企业 is a business or a firm: 大企业 (a big enterprise), 企业家 (an entrepreneur). It is more formal than 公司.

column4: 孩子手里有一个红气球。
column5: The child has a red balloon in his hand.
column6: 气球 is a balloon: 一个气球, 吹气球 (to blow up a balloon). 气 is air.

column5: There is no petrol left in the car.
column6: 汽油 is petrol or gasoline: 加汽油 (to fill up with petrol), 汽油车 (a petrol car).

column5: Please sign here.
column6: 签 is to sign: 签名 (to sign one's name), 签字, 签合同 (to sign a contract). It is also a stick used for drawing lots.

column5: The two companies signed a contract.
column6: 签订 is to formally sign an agreement: 签订合同 (to sign a contract). It is formal; 签 is the everyday word.

column5: Please sign your name here.
column6: 签名 is to sign your name (verb) and a signature (noun): 一个签名 (a signature or autograph).

column5: He signs the contract.
column6: 签字 is to sign a document: 请签字 (please sign), 领导签字 (the leader's signature). 签名 stresses your name; 签字 stresses the act of signing.

column5: We must keep moving forward.
column6: 前进 is to move forward: 向前进 (to move forward), 继续前进 (to keep going forward). It is used for movement and for progress.

column5: Everyone is welcome to come and visit.
column6: 前来 means to come to a place for a purpose, and is formal: 前来参加 (to come and take part), 前来看望 (to come and visit).

column5: His future is bright.
column6: 前途 is future prospects: 前途很好 (a bright future), 有前途 (promising), 没有前途 (with no prospects).

column3: to go to; to head for
column5: They are heading to the railway station.
column6: 前往 is to go to a place, in a formal way: 前往机场 (to head to the airport). It sounds more formal than 去.

column5: This river is shallow.
column6: 浅 means "shallow" (河很浅), "light" in colour (浅蓝, light blue) and "simple" (浅显, easy to understand).

column5: I owe him ten yuan.
column6: 欠 is to owe: 欠钱 (to owe money), 欠你钱 (to owe you money), 还钱 (to pay money back).

column5: There is a picture hanging on the wall.
column6: 墙 is a wall of a house or yard: 一面墙, 墙上 (on the wall).

column5: This country is getting stronger and stronger.
column6: 强大 means strong and powerful: 强大的国家 (a powerful country), 变得强大 (to become strong). 强大 adds a sense of size and power to 强.

column4: 老师强调了安全的重要性。
column5: The teacher stressed the importance of safety.
column6: 强调 is to stress that something is important: 强调重要性 (to stress the importance), 一再强调 (to stress again and again).

column5: The intensity of this exercise is very high.
column6: 强度 is the strength or intensity of something: 运动强度 (exercise intensity), 工作强度 (the intensity of work).

column4: 他对这件事有强烈的兴趣。
column5: He has a strong interest in this matter.
column6: 强烈 means strong and intense: 强烈的感情 (strong feelings), 强烈的要求 (a strong demand), 强烈反对 (to strongly oppose).

column5: The children are fighting over a toy.
column6: 抢 is to grab or snatch (抢东西), to rob, and to rush to get something first (抢票, to rush to buy tickets).

column3: to rescue; to give emergency treatment
column5: The doctors are trying to save the patient.
column6: 抢救 is to rush to save someone or something in danger: 抢救病人 (to give emergency treatment). 救 is "to save"; 抢救 stresses speed.

column5: He quietly walked out of the room.
column6: 悄悄 means quietly or secretly, so as not to be noticed: 悄悄地说 (to say quietly), 悄悄走 (to walk off quietly).

column5: Please cut this apple open.
column6: 切 is to cut with a knife: 切菜 (to chop vegetables), 切开 (to cut open), 切肉 (to slice meat). 剪 is to cut with scissors.

column5: This child is very close to his grandmother.
column6: 亲 means "close, related" (亲人), "dear" (亲爱) and "to kiss" (亲一下).

column5: Dear friends, hello everyone!
column6: 亲爱 means "dear" and comes before 的 and a name or noun: 亲爱的妈妈 (dear Mum). It is how a letter begins.

column4: 他请了很多亲朋好友来参加婚礼。
column5: He invited many relatives and friends to the wedding.
column6: 亲朋好友 means "relatives and friends", all the people close to you. It is a fixed four-character phrase.

column5: The teacher is very warm to us.
column6: 亲切 means warm and kind, making people feel close: 亲切的声音 (a warm voice), 感到亲切 (to feel at home).

column5: Family love is the most important thing.
column6: 亲情 is the love between family members: 亲情很重要, 浓浓的亲情 (deep family love). 爱情 is romantic love.

column5: His family members are all abroad.
column6: 亲人 are the relatives you are close to and love: 想念亲人 (to miss one's family). 家人 is "the family" in everyday speech.

column5: The boss came himself.
column6: 亲自 means in person, doing it yourself: 亲自去 (to go in person), 亲自做 (to do it oneself). It comes before the verb.

column5: He studies very diligently.
column6: 勤奋 means hard-working, especially in study or work: 勤奋学习 (to study diligently), 勤奋的学生 (a diligent student).

column5: These green vegetables are very fresh.
column6: 青 is the colour of fresh plants, between green and blue: 青菜 (green vegetables), 青草 (green grass), 青山 (green hills). It also means young: 青年 (young people).

column5: He will not give up easily.
column6: 轻易 means "easily, lightly", mostly with a negative: 不轻易 (not easily), 轻易相信 (to believe too easily).

column5: In doing things, you must know what matters more.
column6: 轻重 is how light or heavy something is, and also how serious: 知道轻重 (to know what matters), 不知轻重 (to lack judgement).

column4: 这首歌表达了他的情感。
column5: This song has expressed his feelings.
column6: 情感 is emotion and feelings, usually deeper and lasting: 情感丰富 (rich in feelings), 表达情感 (to express emotions). 感情 is similar.

column5: I cannot forget the scene of that day.
column6: 情景 is a scene or situation that you see or remember: 当时的情景 (the scene at the time), 想起那个情景 (to recall that scene).

column5: His mood is not very good today.
column6: 情绪 is your mood or state of feeling: 情绪好 (in a good mood), 控制情绪 (to control one's emotions). 心情 is also "mood", but 情绪 is more about emotional state.

column5: I would like to ask you a question.
column6: 请教 is to ask someone for advice, politely: 请教老师 (to ask a teacher), 向您请教 (to ask for your advice). It is more polite than 问.

column4: 他请求老师再给他一次机会。
column5: He asks the teacher to give him one more chance.
column6: 请求 is to ask politely for something important, or a request: 提出请求 (to make a request), 请求帮助 (to ask for help).

column5: His family was very poor when he was young.
column6: 穷 means poor: 很穷 (very poor), 穷人 (poor people). The opposite is 有钱 (rich).

column4: 这个行业的发展趋势很好。
column5: The development trend of this industry is very good.
column6: 趋势 is a trend or direction of change: 发展趋势 (a trend of development), 上升趋势 (an upward trend).

column5: Parking is not allowed in this area.
column6: 区域 is an area or region: 这个区域 (this area), 工作区域 (a work area). 地区 is similar.

column5: His grandfather passed away last year.
column6: 去世 is a gentle word for "to die", used for people: 他爷爷去世了 (his grandfather has passed away). It is softer than 死.

column5: He has the right to decide this matter.
column6: 权 means "power" or "right": 有权 (to have the right to), 权利 (a right). It is mostly used in words.

column4: 每个孩子都有受教育的权利。
column5: Every child has the right to education.
column6: 权利 is a right: 有权利 (to have the right), 受教育的权利 (the right to education). A duty is 义务.

column5: We will do our best to help you.
column6: 全力 means all one's strength: 全力帮助 (to help with all one's might), 全力准备 (to prepare with all one's strength). It is a noun and an adverb.

column4: 他对这个问题的看法很全面。
column5: His view of this issue is very thorough.
column6: 全面 means comprehensive, covering every side: 全面了解 (to understand fully), 全面检查 (a full check-up).

column4: 全体学生都参加了比赛。
column5: All the students took part in the competition.
column6: 全体 means all of a group: 全体同学 (all the students), 全体人员 (all the staff). It is used for groups of people.

column5: This is a brand-new phone.
column6: 全新 means brand new: 全新的产品 (a brand-new product), 全新的开始 (a completely new start).

column5: His friend urges him to rest earlier.
column6: 劝 is to persuade or advise someone to do or not do something: 劝他 (to persuade him), 劝你别去 (to advise you not to go). It is gentle advice, not an order.

column5: He lacks experience.
column6: 缺乏 is to lack: 缺乏经验 (to lack experience), 缺乏运动 (to lack exercise). It is more formal than 缺少.

column4: 我们要确保孩子的安全。
column5: We must make sure of the children's safety.
column6: 确保 is to make sure that something happens or stays safe: 确保安全 (to ensure safety), 确保质量 (to guarantee quality).

column5: The time has not been fixed yet.
column6: 确定 is to fix or confirm (verb) and "definite" (adjective): 确定时间 (to fix a time), 不确定 (not sure).

column5: Please confirm your name.
column6: 确认 is to check and confirm: 确认信息 (to confirm information). 确认 checks that something is true; 确定 makes something fixed.

column5: A group of children are playing in the yard.
column6: 群 is a measure word for groups: 一群人 (a crowd), 一群鸟 (a flock of birds). As a noun it is a group: 朋友群 (a group chat).

column4: 老年人是一个特殊的群体。
column5: The elderly are a special group.
column6: 群体 is a group of people with something in common: 特殊群体 (a special group), 群体活动 (group activities).

column5: The wood is burning in the fire.
column6: 燃烧 is to burn with a flame: 燃烧汽油 (to burn petrol). 烧 is the everyday word.

column5: We walk around the lake.
column6: 绕 is to go around (绕湖走), to take a roundabout way (绕路) or to wind something (绕线).

column5: He loves music passionately.
column6: 热爱 is to love with strong feeling: 热爱生活 (to love life), 热爱工作 (to love one's job). It is stronger than 爱 or 喜欢.

column5: Rice is high in calories.
column6: 热量 is heat or calories: 食物的热量 (the calories in food), 热量高 (high in calories), 太阳的热量 (the heat of the sun).

column5: Everyone welcomed him warmly.
column6: 热烈 means warm and enthusiastic: 热烈的掌声 (warm applause), 热烈欢迎 (a warm welcome), 讨论热烈 (a lively discussion).

column5: He is a warm-hearted person.
column6: 热心 means warm-hearted and eager to help: 热心人 (a kind helper), 热心帮助 (to help eagerly). 热情 is warm and enthusiastic.

column5: The company needs more talented people.
column6: 人才 is a talented person, or talent in general: 培养人才 (to train talent), 汉语人才 (people skilled in Chinese). It is a collective noun.

column4: 这是人工做的，不是机器做的。
column5: This is made by hand, not by a machine.
column6: 人工 means done by people, not by machines: 人工做 (made by hand). As a noun it also means labour: 人工费 (labour cost).

column5: His relationships with people are very good.
column6: 人际 means between people: 人际关系 (interpersonal relationships), 人际交往 (social interaction). It is almost always used before 关系 or 交往.

column5: This city has a large population.
column6: 人口 is population: 人口很多 (a large population), 城市人口 (the city's population), 人口增加 (population growth).

column5: Humankind needs to protect the environment.
column6: 人类 is humankind: 全人类 (all of humanity), 人类的历史 (the history of humankind). It means people as a species.

column4: 这个工作需要很多人力。
column5: This job needs a lot of manpower.
column6: 人力 is manpower: 人力不够 (not enough workers), 减少人力 (to cut labour).

column5: The people's lives are getting better and better.
column6: 人民 means "the people", a nation's citizens: 人民生活 (the people's life), 为人民服务 (to serve the people).

column5: I have fifty yuan in renminbi.
column6: 人民币 is the Chinese currency, "the people's money". Its unit is 元 or 块: 十元人民币 (ten yuan).

column5: There is a big crowd in the square.
column6: 人群 is a crowd seen as one mass: 走进人群 (to walk into the crowd), 人群中 (in the crowd). 一群人 is "a group of people".

column5: The human body needs water.
column6: 人体 is the human body as a thing: 人体需要水, 人体健康 (the health of the body). 身体 is your body or your health.
